title: Churn retention targeting
summary: Rank active subscribers weekly by risk of cancelling in the next 30 days so the retention team calls the 400 most at-risk customers.
problem: Voluntary churn is 2.1% per month; the retention team calls customers whose contract ends this month, which misses most churners.
decision: Which 400 customers the retention team calls each Monday

success.primary_metric: recall@400 of customers cancelling within 30 days
success.baseline: 0.30 for the current contract-end rule on the same holdout
success.online_metric: saves per 400 calls vs a 5% untreated random holdout over 6 weeks

data.label: voluntary cancellation within 30 days after the Monday scoring date
data.history: 24 months of weekly snapshots, ~50k active customers per week

approach.work: current rule, dummy, logistic regression on a time holdout
LightGBM with point-in-time features; calibrate; pick K=400
score live for 4 weeks without acting; check drift and latency
randomised test: model top-400 vs rule top-400, 6 weeks

milestones.name: Baseline table
milestones.exit: rule, dummy and logistic regression measured

risks.risk: calling customers changes their labels (feedback loop)
support tickets arrive with a 24 h delay
risks.mitigation: use ticket counts up to the previous day only

costs: about 4 person-months to the test readout; serving on the existing batch platform
go_no_go: offline recall@400 >= 0.45 with the 95% CI above the rule
online: +5 saves per week vs the rule with the CI excluding 0
open_questions: Can the retention team handle 500 calls in December?
